purpose: Trust-boundary requirements for third-party data used by Shine applications.
requirements: External provider destinations are explicit HTTPS origins/endpoints controlled by code, not untrusted user input.
Redirects are rejected unless a reviewed provider contract explicitly allows and revalidates them.
Provider requests have bounded deadlines and response bodies are byte-limited before JSON parsing.
Expected response media types and schema-critical fields are validated before data becomes application state.
Coordinates, timestamps, units and other domain-critical context are checked against the request and expected contract.
Provider identity plus retrieval/issue or review timestamps are preserved with the resulting data.
Missing, stale, failed or unverified data stays explicit and is never silently converted to zero, safe, available or current.
Cached provider data has a defined freshness policy and stale fallback is visibly labelled.
Curated legal, rules, access or safety-sensitive records keep an attributable source and review date.
A reviewed source or forecast is not represented as live legal clearance, current closure status, boating safety approval or a prediction of user success.
Only the minimum provider inputs required for the feature are sent; unrelated personal records are not included.
nonClaims: This policy does not prove that an external provider is always correct or available.
This policy does not make historical or reviewed rules current law.
This policy does not turn forecast data into a safety clearance or activity recommendation.
This policy does not certify every external hyperlink as reputable.
